title: The Master Cog & The Braided Beard

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby stepped back from the blueprint and wiped his grease-stained hands on his leather apron.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Up close, you realize Barnaby wasn't fragile like most toy-makers. He was an exceptionally wide, broad-shouldered elf with arms like tree trunks, built like an anvil. His thick beard was long and iron-gray, but he kept it woven into a tight, neat braid tucked securely into his belt so it wouldn't catch in his spinning gears and lathes while he worked.

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: If the Clockmaker stole the Forward Escapement Gear,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: you say, looking at the diagram,

segments.speaker: hero
segments.text: how do we fix the clock? He must have the original locked at the top of the tower.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A sly, stubborn grin broke through Barnaby's braided beard.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The Clockmaker thought he was the only master-smith in Everfrost,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby rumbled with quiet pride.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He forgot who helped him cast the iron.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby walked over to a heavy floor safe hidden beneath an anvil. He spun the brass tumbler—click, click, chunk—and lifted the thick iron lid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Reaching inside with both hands, Barnaby lifted out an object that made the entire workshop glow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It was a magnificent gear wheel forged from solid star-silver and polished brass, eighteen inches wide. Its teeth were cut with microscopic precision, each one inscribed with tiny, glowing golden runes. In the center, a miniature crystal pendulum spun in silent, eternal forward motion.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: For fifty years,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby said softly,

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: I have been in this junkyard, forging a twin. An exact replica of the Master Forward Cog. But I could never install it.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Why not?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip asked, his yellow eyes wide in the golden light.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Because the Great Clock's core rejects ordinary hands,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby explained, looking directly at you.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: If I tried to tune it, the temporal feedback would shatter my mind. Only an Unbound can hold the cog, align its teeth with the Great Wheel, and restart the forward flow of time.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby gently set the glowing cog into an insulated velvet carrying case and handed it to you. The metal felt warm and alive through your gloves, humming with a steady, reassuring heartbeat: tick... tock... tick... tock.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Right at that moment, a massive, earthquake-like rumble shook the cavern floor.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Pip jumped:

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: Great crackers! Was that the Clockmaker?!

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: No,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: a deep, muffled voice whimpered from the open doorway.

segments.speaker: pip
segments.text: That was my belly.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You turn around. Titan was wedged in the workshop doorway, covered in cedar splinters and pine shavings from his feast of wooden goblins. He looked at you with big, mournful puppy eyes and rested his heavy chin on the threshold.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I have vanquished the wooden army,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Titan announced proudly.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All fifty of them. But wood has zero nutritional value, and my stomach is having an emotional crisis. Are there... are there any nubbies in this establishment?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby chuckled, a booming laugh that rattled his braided beard.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A heroic hound deserves a hero's feast,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Barnaby smiled.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Come along, team. Before we march on the Clock Tower, we visit the kitchen. My wife has been expecting us.
